design_rationale: This was an explicitly randomized cluster trial in which nine communities were assigned to test or control by public drawing of envelopes under a constrained randomization scheme.

domain_judgments.rationale: The community-level sequence was genuinely random and concealed until public assignment, but randomization preceded individual recruitment and recruiters knew community allocation, while several baseline imbalances were observed, leaving some concern about recruitment after cluster assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Communities were unaware of their allocation until their name was drawn... Randomization occurred prior to participant recruitment.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention personnel were unblinded, intervention delivery had acknowledged fidelity problems, and analyses were based on participants with observed outcomes rather than a clearly reported intention-to-treat approach, although the primary comparison remained by assigned community.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Mothers and interveners were aware of their community’s allocation... Certainly, challenges related to treatment fidelity are acknowledged.

domain_judgments.rationale: Caries outcomes were available for 241 of 272 recruited pairs (88.6%), with somewhat greater attrition in the test group, and no analysis demonstrating that missingness was unrelated to outcome, though overall retention was fairly high.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: At follow-up, 241 children were examined for caries (110 test, 131 control).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary clinical caries outcome was measured using defined diagnostic criteria by calibrated examiners who were blinded to allocation, making differential measurement unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: When each child was at least 30 mos old, clinical data were collected by calibrated examiners, masked to the community’s assignment.

domain_judgments.rationale: A trial registration and prespecified primary outcome are reported, but no protocol or prespecified analysis plan is provided here to verify all choices, and numerous disease thresholds, adjusted and unadjusted analyses, and exploratory subgroup analyses create some scope for selective emphasis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the primary analysis, caries was defined as the presence of decay (d2 or higher), filling, or extraction due to caries. Additional analyses were performed for various levels of disease.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is judged as some concerns. The strongest protections were explicit cluster randomization and blinded calibrated outcome assessment, but post-randomization recruitment, acknowledged intervention-fidelity issues, modest differential attrition, and incomplete assurance against selective reporting prevent a low-risk judgment.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a stratified blocked randomization sequence generated with a random number generator and assigned 579 dyads 1:1 to MI + ECS or ECS.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was explicitly random, used variable blocks and age stratification, was obtained only after enrollment through off-site telephone assignment, and produced well-balanced baseline groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A stratified blocked randomization design employed a random number generator... Randomization was implemented by telephone between field staff enrolling the participants and a staff member at the University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus. Field staff obtained informed consent and enrolled participants prior to obtaining group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention providers could not be blinded, and the analysis excluded a small unspecified percentage after randomization, although intervention fidelity and adherence were high and longitudinal analyses otherwise followed a modified intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, providers and participants could not be masked in this trial... We call the analysis “modified intention to treat” because a small percentage of the mother-child dyads were dropped after randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome retention was high but not near-complete (84% at 36 months), and the report does not provide sufficient evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcomes or describe a dedicated sensitivity analysis for missing-data bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 579 dyads (290 MI + ECS, 289 ECS) completed the baseline activities, and 84% completed the 36-mo assessment.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary caries outcome was measured identically across groups by calibrated licensed dental professionals who were blinded to allocation, using prespecified objective examination criteria and acceptable interexaminer agreement.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the dmfs measure of decayed, missing, or filled primary tooth surfaces, measured at months 12, 24, and 36, by calibrated dental examiners masked to group assignment... minimum tooth surface-level agreement between each calibrated examiner and the gold standard examiner was a Cohen’s kappa ≥0.75.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial and protocol were prospectively registered/published and the primary outcome and model are described, but the report presents several eligible time-specific and time-averaged contrasts and notes data-driven covariate removal without enough registration detail here to exclude selective analysis reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT01116726)... In addition, simple group comparisons at each assessment, as well as group comparisons that averaged outcomes across all follow-up assessments, were conducted.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is rated some concerns. Randomization and blinded, calibrated outcome measurement were strong, but concerns remain because participants/providers were unblinded, the modified intention-to-treat population excluded some randomized dyads, 16% lacked 36-month assessments without a reported missingness sensitivity analysis, and selective reporting could not be fully excluded.

design_rationale: The study explicitly reports random allocation of mother-child pairs using manual simple randomization by drawing lots.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the sequence was generated by drawing lots and reported complete-case baseline characteristics were broadly similar, allocation concealment was not described and some baseline imbalances were present.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Random sequence generation was performed by manual (simple) randomization via drawing lots.

domain_judgments.rationale: This open-label trial used a per-protocol analysis that excluded randomized participants who did not receive the assigned intervention or lacked follow-up, including post-randomization consent exclusions, rather than analyzing participants as randomized.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The main results are based on the per-protocol analyses.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for only 55 of 75 randomized pairs (73%), with somewhat different completion rates and intervention-related/post-randomization exclusions, and no analysis demonstrated that missingness could not bias the result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of the 75 mother-child pairs included at baseline, 55 (73%) had a complete assessment after 12 months: 28 out of 40 (70%) in the intervention group and 27 out of 35 (77%) in the usual care group.

domain_judgments.rationale: The unblinded outcome assessor measured a partly subjective composite primary outcome incorporating maternal self-reports of behaviors directly targeted by the intervention, making differential assessment or reporting plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Second, the outcome assessor was not blinded to group allocation, which could introduce some degree of detection bias.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was retrospectively registered, and the modified composite risk score and multiple secondary outcomes leave scope for selective choice of outcome definitions or analyses without a prospectively documented analysis plan.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This is a single center, parallel, open-label, usual-care controlled trial with an allocation ratio of 1:1 (retrospectively registered at the Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials [ReBEC]: RBR-74qm3m).

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the per-protocol exclusion of randomized participants, substantial missing outcome data, and unblinded measurement of a partly self-reported and behavior-based primary outcome. Additional concerns arise from unclear allocation concealment and retrospective registration.

design_rationale: The study explicitly used a randomized controlled design and assigned women to test or control groups before consent using Zelen’s design and a random number table.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random-number table was used, but allocation occurred before consent and was disclosed to potential participants, allowing post-randomization refusal or switching; sequence concealment procedures were not otherwise described, although baseline differences were limited.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Zelen’s design with double consent and a random number table (11–13) was used to allocate women into test or control groups before their participation was sought.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants knew their allocation and five control participants switched to the intervention, while the analysis appears based on groups after switching rather than a clearly reported intention-to-treat analysis; however, crossover was small and contamination was considered minimal.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Only five women (0.8%) from all women recruited to the trial changed the group to which they were randomly allocated once they received information about the aims of the trial. All moved from the control group to the test group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for only 70.6% of enrolled participants, retention differed between intervention and control groups, and control-group loss was associated with younger age and lower education, making outcome-dependent bias plausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The overall retention thorough to the examination was 70.6%, higher in the test group (74.4%) than in the control group (66.8%; Table 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: The clinical outcome was measured consistently using prespecified visual criteria, but the sole examiner had also recruited participants and administered the intervention, blinding could fail through recall of allocation, and no reliability assessment was performed for a potentially subjective distinction including noncavitated lesions.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Thirdly, all mothers were recruited and the intervention administered by the same author as who conducted the dental examinations. Any recall of group assignment of individual mothers could have biased the dental observations.

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or prespecified statistical analysis plan is reported, and the paper presents multiple possible outcome definitions and analyses, including noncavitated-plus-cavitated versus cavitation-only disease and adjusted versus unadjusted analyses, leaving scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: If a case definition based on cavitation only was applied, the number of cases shrank to approximately one-quarter.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by substantial and differential missing outcome data with socially patterned attrition in the control group, as well as potentially biased outcome assessment by the investigator who delivered the intervention without documented reliability testing. Additional concerns arise from post-randomization consent/crossover and the absence of a reported prespecified analysis plan.

design_rationale: This was a parallel-group randomized controlled trial using an independently generated random-number sequence, block randomization, and concealed allocation via opaque sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was independently generated using blocked randomization and concealed in opaque sealed envelopes, and measured baseline sociodemographic characteristics were balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The random number sequence was generated in Excel by an independent statistician before recruitment. Randomization with a block size of 4 was adopted, and opaque sealed envelopes were used to conceal the allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and intervention providers were necessarily unblinded in this behavioral intervention, and the report does not describe protocol deviations or an intention-to-treat analysis; reported analyses appear based on available follow-up cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Due to the nature of the intervention, oral health education (OHE) providers and participants could not be masked during this trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 75.2% of randomized families completed the 3-year follow-up, with somewhat different retention by group, and no sensitivity analysis or evidence that missingness was unrelated to outcomes was reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 580 families were recruited at baseline, and 436 toddlers were followed up when they reached 3 y old (test, n = 228; control, n = 208; follow-up rate, 75.2%).

domain_judgments.rationale: Clinical outcomes were measured with standardized methods by blinded, calibrated examiners with high reliability, but parent-reported behavioral outcomes could have been influenced by participants' knowledge of assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Oral examination was carried out by 1 of the 2 trained dentists (W.W. and K.F.Y.) who were blinded to the group allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was registered, the report does not establish that a prespecified analysis plan preceded outcome analysis, and numerous outcomes, time points, thresholds, and data-driven stepwise regression models created scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Independent factors as covariates with a P value <0.40 in the bivariate analyses were selected for the model... Backward stepwise selection was employed to remove insignificant variables from the model.

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven primarily by substantial missing outcome data at 3 years (24.8% attrition) without analyses demonstrating robustness to missingness. Additional concerns arise from lack of participant blinding and available-case analysis, self-reported behavioral outcomes, and potential selective analysis/reporting.
